# <span id="aanchor228"></span> Densitometer Editor

The Densitometer Editor allows users to create densitometers that can be assigned to meters.

Densitometers can be set up to either apply a particular density meter factor (DMF) to a meter or validate the meter’s DMF at import time. The densitometer can also be set up to validate that edited DMF values are within a certain tolerance and the edited value does not vary from the value being replaced by a certain percentage.

Using the densitometer to apply a DMF at import time is useful if the DMF is not being kept up to date in the flow computer in the field. You can create a date time effective DMF entry on a per product basis. As data is imported, FLOWCAL will apply the DMF.

At import time, applying a DMF to a meter will set the DMF characteristic of that meter to the specified value. If a DMF is applied to a meter from the FLOWCAL densitometer and the Uncorrected Observed Density is present and NO Corrected Observed Density is present, a corrected observed density will be calculated from the Uncorrected Observed Density and the applied DMF. If an Uncorrected Observed Density is not available at import, it will be calculated from the Corrected Observed Density and the applied DMF. No action will take place if both the Uncorrected and Corrected Observed Densities are imported, other than updating the DMF. Newly calculated values will be used in calculations for volume and mass accordingly.

Note that the densitometer DMF will only be applied at import. If the product on a batch is edited in the volume editor to a different product, the densitometer will not correct the DMF. The user will need to do that as a manual edit.

The user can choose to validate the DMF at import instead of applying it. When this option is selected if the imported DMF does not match the DMF in the densitometer out to the number of decimal places set in the product editor, FLOWCAL will generate exception 40000.

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Creating a Densitometer</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Creating a Densitometer">

When an entry for a product is created, only a start date is specified. The entry for that product will be used until the end of time or until a new entry for that product is entered. For example: We have created an entry for Crude with a DMF of 0.9500 with an effective date of 1/1/1972 00:00:00. This value will be applied to meter data assigned to this densitometer where the imported product is Crude and the effective date is after 1/1/1972 00:00:00. If a second entry is created with an effective date of 1/1/2012 00:00:00 for Crude, then all data with a product of Crude imported into meters assigned to this densitometer will have this DMF used, provided that the record effective date is 1/1/2012 00:00:00 or later.

<div class="procedure">

To create a densitometer:

1.  Go to **Setup** \> **Densitometer**.
2.  Click **New** or press **Alt+N**.
3.  Enter a densitometer name.
4.  Click **Save**.
5.  Right-click and select **New Periodic** to add a new periodic record.
6.  Click **Save**.

</div>

Additional product entries can be created for a densitometer. For instance, there might be a different crude product that flows on a meter such as Light Crude. Creating an entry for Light Crude at 1/1/2012 01:00:00 will cause all Light Crude data on meters assigned to this densitometer with an effective date on or after 1/1/2012 00:00:00 to apply the specified DMF.

Meter data with a product of Crude will still use the entry for Crude. For a given date there can be only one entry in the densitometer. If a pyc is done for multiple products at the same time, each product entry must be entered at least one second apart from the other.

</div>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Editing a Densitometer">

<div class="procedure">

To edit a densitometer:

1.  Go to **Setup** \> **Densitometer**.
2.  Select a densitometer.
3.  Click the **Periodic** tab and double-click a periodic record.
4.  Make changes to the densitometer data as needed.
5.  Click **Save**.

</div>

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Deleting a Densitometer">

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Deleting a Densitometer">

<div class="procedure">

To delete a densitometer:

1.  Go to **Setup** \> **Densitometer**.
2.  Select a densitometer.
3.  Go to **Densitometer** \> **Delete**.

</div>

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Densitometer Assignment">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Densitometer Assignment</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Densitometer Assignment">

Use the Densitometer Assignment screen to assign meters to the densitometer so that the DMF can either be applied or validated during import.

<div class="procedure">

##### Applying a DMF to Meter Data

1.  Go to **Setup** \> **Densitometer**.

2.  Select a densitometer.

3.  Click the **Assignment** tab.

4.  Right-click and select **New Assignment**.

5.  Select a meter from the drop-down menu.

6.  Select an apply option. If you choose Apply DMF to meter you must also select a recalc method. If you choose Validate meter DMF, then the DMF wil not be applied to the meter, but the meter’s imported DMF will be validated against the DMF in the densitometer. If you choose Unspecified, then no action will take place.

    If the Apply option for a densitometer assignment is set to "Apply DMF to meter", the DMF is applied to the meter batch on import. An observed density is calculated from the unobserved density and the DMF is applied to the meter and calculations proceed accordingly.

7.  Enter an effective date.

8.  Click **Save**.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 360;height: 301;" />

</div>

</div>
